units.translation: May Zeus, who disposes all things, never set power hostile to my will.
With self-willed (thus I corrected for 'private') judgment you honor mortals too much, Prometheus.
And some one of the gods has taken hold of my judgment.
I would not boast that I am a supreme judge of prophecies.
And I made known to them the hard-to-interpret omens.
i.e. friend, intimate: in which sense γνωτός [known] is more probable, as the Homeric examples collected in the Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 694 show.
To strangers so fortunate, for the sake of their good fortunes, I would have wished to become known and to be received as a guest.

γοᾶται [he wails] at Ch. 632 is suspect, where the sense seems rather to require βοᾶται [he shouts], which Blomfield conjectured, a conjecture however uncertain, since the neighboring words are corrupt. The active form γοᾶν [to wail], which the epic poets use, I restored at Pers. 676, where in M is read, ὦ πολύκλαυτε φίλοισι θανὼν | τί τάδε δυνάτα δυνάτα | περὶ τᾶι σᾶι δίδυμα διαγόεν ἁμαρτία [O much-lamented, dead to your friends, why these mighty, mighty twin errors of yours...], which I corrected thus, ὦ πολύκλαυτε θανὼν δυνάστα, | τί τάδε φίλοισι περίβαλες | δίδυμα γοᾶν ἁμάρτια [O much-lamented ruler, dead, why did you cast upon your friends these twin errors of wailing], about which I spoke in Philologus vol. 13 p. 491.
O much-lamented, dead to your friends, why these mighty, mighty twin errors of yours...
O much-lamented ruler, dead, why did you cast upon your friends these twin errors of wailing
which is corrupted into στρογγύλων [round] in the inferior manuscripts of Strabo 4 p. 182.
which the scholiast explains as τῶν γόων τὸ ἄνθος ἀποδρέπομαι [I pluck the flower of lamentations].

It is a word peculiar to Aeschylus, which in M is consistently proparoxytone γόεδνος [lamentable]. I wrote γοεδνός [lamentable] with I. G. Schneider, with which accent similar adjectives are written κεδνός παιδνός ψεδνός [careful, childish, thin-haired], about which Herodian partly spoke in vol. 1 p. 172 ed. Lentz.
Answer the strangers with reverent, lamentable, and Zagrean words.
I pluck the flower of lamentations
Thus Hermann for γοήτων ( γοητῶν Μ corrected ) νόμον μεθήσομεν [we will send forth the wailers' song].
We will establish a plucked wailing song.
we will send forth the song
in a verse, as it seems, spurious,
as from the scholiast's annotation it was corrected for ἄτην γε μείζω καὶ μέγ᾽ ἐμπλήσας γόμου γόμος [a greater ruin and having filled a great cargo] γόμος [cargo] for δόμος [house] Blomf. Ag. 1011.
Filling with ruin and having loaded a great cargo.
a greater ruin and having filled a great cargo
And with a bolt-fastened plank you destroy utterly.
